title: Runtime failure lighthouse and telemetry routing spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: define and implement a compact, actionable failure taxonomy (the 'Lighthouse') and routing rules for enriched telemetry so the Console shows deterministic, SLO-oriented error signposts for production inference flows. Scope: tracing hooks, span enrichment rules, metrics + logs forwarding, OLAP schema for error slices, and a dashboard wire that surfaces timeouts, overload, model-level errors (model-reject/invalid-output), transport errors (HTTP/gRPC codes), and degradation signals (high tail-latency, retries, queueing).

Goals:
- Create a small, mutually-exclusive taxonomy that maps runtime observations to root causes: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_FAILURE, TRANSPORT_ERROR, CONFIG/DEPLOY, and UNKNOWN.
- Define span/tagging conventions for the runtime and gateway so the Console's error panels can attribute incidents to taxonomy buckets without heavy sampling.
- Specify telemetry routing: high-cardinality traces go to low-ttl hot store for 24h; aggregated failure counters and provenance indices to OLAP (30d); full payload traces for sampled incidents to long-term trace storage on-demand.
- Build SLO-aware alerting signals (burn rates + cardinality) and dashboard panes optimized for quick Triage: top affected routes, model variants, host pools, and latency percentiles by failure bucket.

Non-Goals:
- Replacing existing incident runbooks; this work should feed them.
- Implementing new security controls beyond tagging/KMS integration already planned.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A documented taxonomy in Confluence with unambiguous mapping rules and examples for each bucket.
2) Instrumentation PRs merged in runtime + gateway that add the agreed span tags (span.tag.failure_bucket, span.tag.model_version, span.tag.queue_time_ms).
3) Telemetry routing config committed for Kafka topics + OLAP table schemas and a small ETL notebook that produces the failure slice materialized view.
4) Console dashboard prototype that shows failure buckets for last 1h/24h/7d, top 10 routes by failure rate, and a drilldown link that opens an enriched trace sample.
5) E2E test plan and a canary rollout to 5% of traffic with synthetic fault injection demonstrating correct attribution.

Planned workstreams:
- Design: finalize taxonomy with PM and SRE; mock dashboard panels. (Owner: Diego)
- Runtime instrumentation: add span enrichment hooks and prefix/KV cache markers. (Owner: Priya Kaur)
- Gateway changes: propagate transport codes and queueing metrics. (Owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- Pipeline: Kafka topic routing + OLAP schema + aggregation jobs. (Owner: Linh Nguyen)
- Console: dashboard panels, drilldown UX, alerting rules. (Owner: Diego)

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: high-cardinality tags causing OLAP cost blowup. Mitigation: hash and bucket high-cardinality identifiers, cap route cardinality at pipeline layer.
Risk: misclassification of transient 5xx as MODEL_FAILURE. Mitigation: add simple hysteresis heuristic (require 3 occurrences in 30s window) before marking model bucket.
next_steps: 1) SRE retention sign-off (ENG-246802). 2) Reduce route cardinality mapping and push pipeline config to staging. 3) Schedule 5% canary and observe attribution correctness for 48h. 4) After canary, move dashboard to beta release in console-2026.04.
